metas.name: Cure
metas.description: Kiyoshi Kurosawa's Japanese thriller about a detective chasing murders committed by ordinary people who don't know why they did it. Hypnotic and deeply unsettling.

metas.name: Compliance
metas.description: Based on a true story: a prank caller posing as a cop talks fast-food staff into abusing a coworker. A study of ordinary people obeying something monstrous.

metas.name: Confessions
metas.description: Tetsuya Nakashima's Japanese film about a teacher who calmly tells her class that two students killed her daughter, and that she has already taken revenge. Icy and stylish.

metas.name: Snowtown
metas.description: Based on Australia's worst serial killings: a charismatic neighbor draws a teenager into his circle of killers. Quiet, horrifying and real.

metas.name: Kill List
metas.description: Ben Wheatley's British film about two ex-soldiers turned hitmen whose latest job is getting stranger. It moves from kitchen-sink drama into nightmare, with a bleak final turn.

metas.name: Cheap Thrills
metas.description: A broke father meets an old friend at a bar, where a rich couple starts paying them for ever-worse dares. Escalation turned into a dark comedy.

metas.name: Big Bad Wolves
metas.description: In this Israeli thriller, a vigilante cop and a grieving father kidnap a suspected child killer. Brutal and unexpectedly funny, with a final shot that bites.

metas.name: Dogtooth
metas.description: Yorgos Lanthimos's Greek breakthrough about parents who keep their grown children sealed in a compound of invented rules. Cruel, deadpan and very strange.

metas.name: Man Bites Dog
metas.description: A Belgian mockumentary in which a film crew follows a charming serial killer and slowly becomes his accomplice. Pitch-black satire played straight.

metas.name: The Hunt
metas.description: A Danish kindergarten teacher is falsely accused, and his small town turns on him. Thomas Vinterberg's portrait of a community's cruelty is agonizingly tense.
